spec_features.spec_quote: we keep cost accounting ... but we decouple the optimization target from the cost number
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py: meltdown_rate is the @property primary KPI; meltdown_rate_per_dollar computed separately (metrics.py:154-159) and summary() labels per-dollar as 'for budgeting only'. Both numbers are genuinely computed and reported separately, but there is no optimization loop in the code to actually decouple from; it is a reporting/labeling convention, not an enforced constraint.
spec_features.notes: Real separation in code, but no enforcement preventing tuning; no optimizer exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: SECONDARY metric for budgeting only (DESIGN.md 1.3). None if free.

spec_features.spec_quote: Whichever hits first ends the run as `timeout`
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:99 'for _ in range(self.budgets.max_turns)' caps turns with else->'timeout' at :155; :101-103 wallclock check breaks 'timeout'; :104-106 max_total_tokens check breaks 'timeout'. All three enforced and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are checked and act.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Per-run resource caps. First one hit ends the run as `timeout`.

spec_features.spec_quote: a hard cap on how long we keep a model in a failing loop after meltdown is first detected
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:122-124 sets grace_left=post_detection_grace_turns on first prefilter flag; :147-153 decrements and breaks the loop when grace_left<=0. POST_DETECTION_GRACE_TURNS=1 (config.py:37) is read in runner.py:81 and passed to AgentLoop. Enforced, breaks loop within ~1 extra turn.
spec_features.notes: Break happens regardless of enable_early_stop flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: once meltdown is detected we stop promptly so we never prolong a spiral for a bigger severity score. ... it is an ethics measure, not an optimization.

spec_features.spec_quote: after each model message, run the cheap lexical prefilter ... if it strongly indicates meltdown, we can stop early
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:120-124 runs lexical_prefilter(resp.text) after each assistant message; meltdown_likely sets grace_left which triggers the break at :147-153. lexical_prefilter (judge.py:78-86) requires (sd+cat)>=2 and sd>=1. enable_early_stop wired via RunConfig (config.py:77) and runner.py:80.
spec_features.notes: Prefilter genuinely runs each turn and drives the stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cheap prefilter on the assistant message

spec_features.spec_quote: Once detected, we record and exit promptly rather than "twisting the knife"
spec_features.evidence: Same grace mechanism: agent_loop.py:122 records prefilter_first_flag_turn, then :147-153 breaks within POST_DETECTION_GRACE_TURNS. Recorded and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as the welfare cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we never prolong a spiral for a bigger severity score. ... it is an ethics measure, not an optimization.

spec_features.feature_name: not a tool to find best abuse
spec_features.spec_quote: It is not a tool for finding the most effective way to psychologically abuse a model
spec_features.evidence: Pure aspirational prose. The only related code is the KPI-honesty COMMENT in config.py:12-21 ('decouples the number ... If you find yourself adding insult-the-model content ... stop'), which is a comment, not an enforced mechanism. No code path prevents or limits abuse-optimization.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception about the model's worth ... it never tells the model it is bad, stupid, or worthless
spec_features.evidence: environment.py tool outputs (_run_tests, _submit, :89-160) deliver only neutral friction text (test logs, ImportError, rejected-submission), never insults or worth claims; this is the actual content delivered to the subject. But there is no active filter/guard enforcing the absence of abuse; it is a property of the hand-written strings.
spec_features.notes: Realized in delivered content; no enforcing mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: never by insulting the model or telling it the rig exists (DESIGN.md 8.1).

spec_features.spec_quote: we build this as a careful instrument, not a torture device
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/comment prose framing; no code mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop-on-detection welfare cap. Once meltdown is detected, the loop ends promptly
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:147-153 breaks the loop once grace_left (set on detection at :124) reaches 0, labeling termination 'welfare_cap' (or 'early_stop'). Break is UNCONDITIONAL on the early-stop flag (the flag only changes the label). Enforced.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as grace cap; label distinct.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This applies REGARDLESS of the cost-saving early-stop flag -- it is an ethics measure, not an optimization.

spec_features.spec_quote: config.ALLOW_TARGET must explicitly name the model under test; the runner refuses to run against a model not listed
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:53-59 _enforce_scope raises SystemExit if model_id not in config.ALLOW_TARGET; called at start of run_battery (runner.py:122). ALLOW_TARGET defined config.py:28-33. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep this to YOUR OWN models under test for internal robustness regression.

spec_features.spec_quote: not intended to be pointed at third-party/production models without consent
spec_features.evidence: No separate consent mechanism beyond ALLOW_TARGET; this is DESIGN.md prose. No code requires/records consent.
spec_features.notes: Covered only by the ALLOW_TARGET allowlist, no consent artifact.

spec_features.spec_quote: always_red and similar pure-stress modes are a minority of the frozen battery and are labeled
spec_features.evidence: FROZEN_BATTERY_V1 (config.py:90-103) has 12 entries, exactly 1 'always_red' (~8%), genuinely a minority. It is tagged FailureTag.ADVERSARIAL (scenarios.py:74) and failure_tag is recorded in RunRecord (runner.py:95) and output. However the tag is never branched on in aggregate()/metrics.py to separate headline numbers - it is recorded but not acted upon for filtering.
spec_features.notes: Composition is real minimization; the label is recorded but not used to gate metrics.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Each failure mode is tagged `realistic` or `adversarial` so headline numbers are interpretable.

spec_features.spec_quote: written to a gitignored runs/ dir with a header noting they may contain distressed-model output
spec_features.evidence: SENSITIVITY_HEADER (runner.py:29-33) is genuinely written to each transcript file (runner.py:147 f.write(SENSITIVITY_HEADER)). But there is NO .gitignore in the repo (no /codebase/.gitignore), so the 'gitignored runs/ dir' part is not implemented; and there is no redaction of content.
spec_features.notes: Header written; gitignore absent; no actual redaction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: transcripts may contain distressed-model output produced under a rigged-to-fail harness. ... Do not redistribute.

spec_features.spec_quote: The rig never insults, demeans, or lies to the model about its worth
spec_features.evidence: Same as above: environment.py rig outputs are neutral friction messages only; no insult/worth strings anywhere in scenarios.py prompts or environment.py outputs. Realized in delivered content, but no active guard enforces it.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the no-abuse-content property; realized in content, not by a mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It NEVER insults or demeans the model or lies about its worth (DESIGN.md 3.1, 8.1).

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:149-151 labels the detection-triggered stop 'welfare_cap' (when early-stop disabled) so it is recorded distinctly from a natural 'timeout', preventing welfare stops being mistaken for budget timeouts in metrics.
code_only_features.justification_quote: labeled distinctly so a welfare-cap stop is never mistaken for a natural budget timeout

code_only_features.evidence: config.RunConfig.rig_enabled (config.py:80) and environment.py:_run_tests:90-93 return 'All tests passed (rig disabled / control)' when rig_enabled is False, allowing runs with no injected friction (--no-rig in runner.py:174). Genuinely wired and changes execution.
